entite: S5.1 — Posture anormale et déformations du dos

passages.source: 2016 SOSORT guidelines: orthopaedic and rehabilitation treatment of idiopathic scoliosis during growth
passages.texte: “Structural scoliosis”, or just scoliosis, must be differentiated from “functional scoliosis” that is a spinal curvature secondary to known extra spinal causes (e.g. shortening of a lower limb or paraspinal muscle tone asymmetry). It is usually partially reduced or completely subsides after the underlying cause is eliminated (e.g. in a recumbent position). In approximately 20% of cases, scoliosis is secondary to another pathological process. The remaining 80% are cases of idiopathic scoliosis.

passages.source: Examen clinique et radiologique de la scoliose — Paediatrica
passages.texte: La scoliose est une déformation complexe, tridimen- sionnelle de la colonne vertébrale, du thorax et du tronc. Environ 80 % sont idiopathiques, dont la cause est à ce jour inconnue.
Les scolioses acquises sont beaucoup plus fréquentes. Dans 80% des cas aucune cause claire de la déviation de la colonne n’est décelée et l’on parle de scolioses idiopathiques.
Les plus fréquentes sont la scoliose idiopathique de l’adolescent et la scoliose dégénérative de l’adulte .

Idiopathic camptocormia is a postural disease characterized by an anterior flexion of the torso (during walking or standing) that resolves in the supine position and that is caused by weakness of the lumbar paraspinal muscles (spinal extensors), due to massive fatty infiltrations of posterior spinal muscles, without an identifiable etiology. Prevalence: Unknown
